tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Sylvester's Law of Inertia]

↗ cor:scalar-product-signature-form

1. ch2:2.65

If a finite-dimensional scalar product $q$ has the normal form (2.23), then $r$ is the maximum dimension of a subspace on which $q$ is positive definite. Consequently $r$ and $s$ are independent of the chosen basis.

Proof

↗ cor:scalar-product-signature-form \sketch Let $(b_i)$ be the orthonormal basis dual to $(\beta ^i)$. The span of $b_1,\ldots ,b_r$ is positive definite, so the maximum is at least $r$. On $N=\operatorname {span}(b_{r+1},\ldots ,b_{r+s})$, the form is nonpositive. Any positive-definite subspace $W$ has $W\cap N=\{ 0\} $, hence $\dim W+s\leq r+s$ and $\dim W\leq r$. Thus $r$ has a basis-free characterization, and $s=\dim V-r$.

□
